items.toString:
This change aligns Phoenix’s day-boundary logic around Bulgarian business time while storing real instants in UTC. For *Accounting Period*, Start and End must be persisted in UTC as the DST-aware equivalents of *00:00 BG* on the 1st and *23:59 BG* on the last day of the month, and all lookup, close, and eligibility checks must compare UTC instants to those bounds—not naive midnight UTC. For *Payment*, the full EasyPay {{DATE}} timestamp must be kept, converted to UTC, and used to derive the BG payment day for packaging and period assignment instead of dropping the time. For *Payment Package*, the nightly lock must run at *Bulgarian midnight* (21:00 UTC in summer) and lock packages for the BG business day that just ended. Together, these updates prevent near-midnight payments from landing in the wrong package, Accounting Period, or lock window, with a controlled historical reassignment step for in-scope transactions already posted under the old rules.

For more information, please, see the attached file.

hi, we've started working on this issue but it needs time for development and the QA as well, since it's a risky change. It won't be ready for tomorrow's PROD update, so I propose planning a separate update for this one.

Hi again,
A few notes and one question on this change:
1. We will take both the date and time from the payment key and convert them to UTC. That means the field type will change from DATE to DATETIME. The change will apply automatically to all existing payments. For payments other than EasyPay, the time will be set to 00:00. (For EasyPay Payments we will try to capture exact times)
2. In the past Accounting Periods were opened and closed manually by users in Bulgaria. After the UTC conversion, only the display will change; accounting periods for existing transactions will not change. (That's a good thing)
3. Question - Should we update Payment Packages for already existing payments after we change the locking time?
